svg.title: Adding one real observation produces a quadratic population variance with an exact interval
svg.desc: The original numerical observations are one, four and seven. Their mean is four and population variance six. Adding a real observation t gives four records, total twelve plus t and sum of squares sixty-six plus t squared. The new population variance is sixty-six plus t squared divided by four, minus the square of twelve plus t divided by four. Completing the square gives nine halves plus three sixteenths times t minus four squared. Thus the minimum variance is nine halves at t equal to four. The graph is an upward parabola with vertex four, nine halves. Its intersections with variance six are t equal to four minus two square root two and four plus two square root two. The variance is at most six on the closed interval between these values. The endpoints are filled because equality is included. All real t are allowed; only a finite window is drawn.
